title: Envisioning the future of education technology
author: Envisioning
frame: Vertical timeline with labelled years 2012, 2020, 2030 and 2040 on the left and alternating light/dark horizontal bands, one band per year: 7 bands between the 2012 and 2020 bands, 9 between 2020 and 2030, 9 between 2030 and 2040. The scale compresses with distance (about 80px per year in 2013-2020, 62px in 2021-2030, 52px in 2031-2040 on the 2480px image). The top band holding the 2012 label is taller (y 421-657) and is read as 2012 for every node in it. Each leaf technology circle is read at the year band that contains its centre; a centre within 4px of a band boundary is read as the later year and marked low confidence. Hub circles (Digitized classrooms, Gamification, Opening of information, Disintermediation, Tangible computing, Virtual/physical studios) are concepts, not placements, and are recorded only as each leaf's category (by circle colour).
quote: This visualization attempts to organize a series of emerging technologies that are likely to influence education in the upcoming decades. Despite its inherently speculative nature, the driving trends behind the technologies can already be observed, meaning it's a matter of time before these scenarios start panning out in learning environments around the world.

notes: Read from the 1753x2480 poster image served by envisioning.com, cross-checked against the archived June 2012 PDF (PDF creation date 2012-06-26; earliest archived page 2012-06-28), whose text layer gave label positions; the two layouts match. The PDF footer credits envisioningtech.com, tferesearch.com and Marie Curie FP7; the 2012 web page calls it a collaboration between TFE Research and Envisioning. The image version replaces the footer quote with an 'envisioning.io/education' box; node positions are unchanged. The poster never says what a placement year means: it speaks of technologies 'likely to influence education in the upcoming decades' and scenarios that 'start panning out in learning environments'. So 'becomes mainstream around year Y' is this file's reading, not the poster's wording; a placement is closer to 'starts to influence learning environments around Y'. Placements are also not technology-wide: they concern use in education (e.g. Tablets in classrooms, 3D printers in schools). Column headers (Classroom / Studio / Virtual) are loose zones, not a grid, and are not recorded per entry. Numbered grey captions (1-6) describe a progression from fixed classroom IT (1) to continuous, interconnected education (6) and are not placements. The envisioning.com page returned HTTP 429 to automated fetches on 2026-10-01 and is unlisted in its CMS; the web.archive.org snapshots are the stable sources.
